<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **51** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/mcp/README.md`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/index.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**25** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 128b6571f476d4fae347d8f860b04b95927d2cce`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/mcp/README.md`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/index.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **14** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **55** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 128b6571f476d4fae347d8f860b04b95927d2cce` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7a64a05ba29b0af6b99891bf5f52ad189cb9fe24` — the merge of head `b6acbd9a9b1148565de3aa69a6334b020019674a` into base `128b6571f476d4fae347d8f860b04b95927d2cce`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7a64a05ba29b0af6b99891bf5f52ad189cb9fe24 && git checkout 7a64a05ba29b0af6b99891bf5f52ad189cb9fe24
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 128b6571f476d4fae347d8f860b04b95927d2cce b6acbd9a9b1148565de3aa69a6334b020019674a && git checkout -B drift-repro 128b6571f476d4fae347d8f860b04b95927d2cce && git merge --no-ff b6acbd9a9b1148565de3aa69a6334b020019674a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 128b6571f476d4fae347d8f860b04b95927d2cce
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 128b6571f476d4fae347d8f860b04b95927d2cce` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `7fd55e60c190a656024a336e92019ea930535bae`
Local-runs: none

Face: declaration. `record-recognisers --paths` reads no published-schema or governed path off the file list, and the changeset and the PR body carry `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. Rendered by an isolated sub-agent of this seat. Inputs: card #32442 with every comment (ruling A 6837430865, acceptance 6846046224, ruling 1B + 2B 6849636735, claim 6849988930, report 6856567007), the PR body, the net diff against `main` (merge-base `a596c03c`), the check-runs on the head and, for the two red lanes, on the merge-base and on `main`. Code outside the diff was read, never reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

**Right**

1. **Read admission** (`packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts`). `readGuard` is `guard` with one exception: a `sys_` name the bridge attests. It fails closed three ways (no bridge member, a throw, any answer but the boolean `true`). `describe_object`, `query_records`, `aggregate_records` and `get_record` take it, and `list_objects` filters by the same attestation. Read at the head: `validate_expression`, `create_record`, `update_record`, `delete_record`, the bulk delete, `read_file` and `create_upload_link` still call `guard`. No MCP write opens on any `sys_*` object.
2. **Attestation.** Both bridges answer with `isAiReadExposed` over the unmasked served definition: the stored-metadata family is refused before the key is read, a non-`sys_` name never answers true, only the boolean `true` opens. One object in the tree declares the key (`sys_approval_request`); `sys_approval_action` declares nothing; an object extension is a strict shape with no `enable` key. No other `sys_*` object becomes readable through this door. `McpDataBridge.aiReadExposed` is an optional member, additive on the published type.
3. **2B cannot widen** (`request-read-gate.ts`). The split takes out only a conjunctive `pending_approvers: { $contains: own id }` (the root, or a root `$and`); a pin under `$or` or `$not`, another id, or a second operator is left as written. The conjunct becomes `id in waitingOnCallerIds`, and the participant conjunct is still ANDed at the root after it, so every answer is a subset of what the same caller's untargeted read serves. `waitingOnCallerIds` is `approverRequestIds(actingAddresses(caller))`, the call `visibleRequestIds` makes for its current-approver arm: no second fold. A caller pinning another id gets that literal inside their own participant set. A throw, or a source without the member, denies the read. An emptied `$and` is the AND identity in the SQL driver. The rewrite is off on the child tables (`column === 'id'`).
4. **1B, a member party to no request reads no row**, on each path the grant opens, read at the head. The gate covers `find`, `findOne`, `count` and `aggregate`, which is the engine's whole read set, and each path below reaches the engine as the caller: REST list, by id, count and grouped; `$expand` sub-reads (`expandRelatedRecords` re-enters `find`); the cross-object search (`searchAll` reads through `find`); ad-hoc analytics (the native-SQL strategy declines an object that carries an engine middleware, #21080, and the ObjectQL strategy hands the query to `engine.aggregate`); a `ReadableIds` leaf over this parent is refused by the engine (the object-scoped-middleware class); export asks `canExport` first and the baseline grants no `allowExport`; the MCP tools go through `callData`. No REST write opens on the approval objects: the line is read-only, `apiMethods` is `get` / `list`, `sys_approval_action` and `sys_approval_approver` are not named, and `external_default` gets no line.
5. **Tool text.** `{current_user_id}` is resolved by the engine for every `where`, so the new general sentence in `query_records` holds beyond this object.

**Must-fix**

- **A. CI on the head is red on two lanes, both the diff's own.** The merge-base `a596c03c` and `main` `e997113c` are green on both.
  - `Type Check · workspace` (and its aggregate `TypeScript Type Check`): `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` `check:test-typecheck` reports `src/request-read-waiting-on-caller.integration.test.ts: 2 type error(s) in a file the ledger does not cover`. It arrived with `7fd55e60c` (`as any` replaced by `satisfies EngineQueryOptions`). The PR body's "plugin-approvals typecheck exit 0" does not hold on this head.
  - `Test Core (6/8)`: `packages/verify/src/action-door-api-forward-denied-subject.test.ts:174`, "the control: the approver cannot read the request row through the data door", expects `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`. 1B makes that read succeed, and the diff does not move the pin. The file's header and the comment at `packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts:4022-4028` carry the same sentence ("a member has no data-door read on `sys_approval_request` by design").
- **B. A merge-queue-only pin that 1B reverses and the diff does not touch:** `packages/qa/dogfood/test/approval-request-schema-party-read.dogfood.test.ts` (decision 6840464379). With the baseline grant, three of its four stars stop holding for `sys_approval_request`: a member party to no request answered `404` on the definition and not shown it in the object list; the approver's object list being that member's plus exactly the two declared objects; the approver's data reads of the request refused. Read from code, not from a run: the dogfood shards first run in the merge queue, so this reds the queue, not the PR. Move the pins, and say in the PR which terms of 6840464379 the 1B ruling supersedes and which stand (`sys_approval_action`).
- **C. Security findings: one, withheld (reported to the seat).** It bears on the "field masking still applies" line of the acceptance notes.

**Should-fix**

- **D. Sentences the diff makes false and leaves in place:** `sys-approval-request.object.ts:48-56`, in a file this PR edits ("the data side is closed to ordinary members on purpose", "the rows stay closed"); the no-middleware-seam warning in `approvals-plugin.ts` ("Grant no read on those objects to non-administrators", which the baseline now does). The published spec prose says the same (`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts:3870` and the `schemaReadDelegate` describe string): a follow-up card for the spec lane, not this PR.
- **E. `list_objects` cost.** Each listed `sys_*` object is attested through the HTTP bridge's `readServedObject`, which is one full merged `getMetaItems({ type: 'object' })` read per object, all at once (`filterAsync`). For an administrator that is every system object, on the first call of every agent session. The listing already in hand can answer it: attest from one read, or memoize per request. Read from code, not measured.

**Nit**

- The `query_records` description in `@objectstack/mcp` now names one plugin's object and column. "Where the app has approvals" covers the stack without the plugin; the sentence would sit more naturally on the object's own description.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/mcp-read-tools-ai-readable-system-object.md` names `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` and `@objectstack/plugin-security` at `patch`: the four published packages the diff moves (the dogfood package is private).

- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right. Every change widens an accept set (the read tools' object set, the member baseline, the answer to the waiting-on-me filter) and nothing narrows.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right. No key, value or type an author can write is added or changed. `enable.aiReadable` was published by #32971 with this meaning, and this PR is its first reader.
- By AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3, `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. Both lines are line-initial in the PR body and in the changeset body. `Check Changeset` is green. The level is correct.

Prose, which is not this record's face and is named because the brief asked: `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx` is updated and agrees with the diff ("by team" holds through the open-time expansion of a team slot, as the PR body says; an unstaffed `team:` literal is not an acting address). `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx` now states something false in two places: `:593-602` ("`sys_approval_request` and `sys_approval_action` are closed to ordinary members on the data side", "A member who can see none is answered `404`", "a member the data door refuses still reaches the rows only through `/api/v1/approvals/*`") and `:858-861` ("although the data API stays closed to them on the approval objects"). The docs-drift check listed that page. For the lane seat's ACCEPT.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Report 6856567007 carries `open_questions: []` and no dev flag, so there is nothing to answer there. It carries no `security_findings` line either; see C.
- **Ruling wording against the path.** 6849636735 says "plugin-approvals grants"; the grant is a line in plugin-security's `member_default`, as claim 6849988930 names it (seat-approved, the #30108 shape). Accepted as claimed. To keep in view: the grant ships in one plugin and its row authority is bound in another's `start()`.
- **Derived surfaces 1B opens that the PR body does not name**, each read as gated (① 4): the metadata API serves the `sys_approval_request` definition, and the object list names it, to every member (B); the cross-object search sweeps it; an ad-hoc analytics query over it is admitted. The seat's ACCEPT should name them.
- One further flag travels with the withheld finding (reported to the seat).
- **Verification claims against the head.** The body's "103 derived, 103 run, every recorded exit 0" and "plugin-approvals typecheck exit 0" do not match the check-runs (A). The `packages/verify` suite that holds the reversed pin was not among what was run; if `dispatch-gates` derives no verify or dogfood family from a change to `default-permission-sets.ts`, that is a gap for the tooling lane.
- The new dogfood file, the evidence for the red lines over the live transport, has not run in CI on this head (the shards are skipped on a PR). Its last cited local run is on `5b91c3641b`.
- `Test Core (1/8)` was still in progress when this record was written: six shards green, 6/8 red.
- Author: the PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.
- The PR body names triage#1 for this review. No `Contract-review-claim:` line and no earlier record names this head on the PR or on the card; the request on #32588 (6856591303) is unanswered.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-bb7kzf`
Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4cwJbS8sZAfru2iyvQq`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

Must-fix: A (two red lanes), B (the queue pin), C (withheld). Should-fix: D, E. A delta review by the same reviewer is owed on the next head.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `8e4da801d2578d70f624ca6d8b4c2a63bb9615c0`
Local-runs: probe — GHSA-2985-5f64-8wgh: the diff and the check-runs could not settle whether its fix on this head is complete. Two throwaway test files in a detached checkout of this head (one on the PR's own dogfood rig, one beside the plugin-audit suite), deleted after the run; the worktree is clean and nothing was committed. The same build ran the two approval dogfood files the PR lanes skip.

This is a DELTA record on round 1 (6857191533, FAIL at `7fd55e60c1`). It judges `git diff 7fd55e60c1 8e4da801d2` (four commits, 15 files) and the code that diff touches, item by item against round 1, and says nothing about a later head. Face: declaration, unchanged. The file list carries no published-schema or governed path, and the changeset and the PR body carry `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. Rendered by the same isolated sub-agent of this seat. Inputs: round 1, the claim re-post 6857527959, the fix report as the seat relayed it (it is not on the card), the PR body, the delta, and the check-runs on this head. Code outside the diff was read, never reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

**Round-1 items**

- **A. Closed.** `Type Check · workspace`, `TypeScript Type Check` and `Test Core (6/8)` are green on this head.
  - `request-read-waiting-on-caller.integration.test.ts` types its count and aggregate options with `EngineCountOptions` and `EngineAggregateOptions`.
  - The verify control is re-grounded, not flipped. `action-door-api-forward-denied-subject.test.ts` boots the shipped default sets with one line withdrawn, `member_default`'s `sys_approval_request`, and a module-top guard throws when the baseline stops naming the table. The control still expects `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` on the data door, so every decision the file pins is still a forward that authorizes while the load is denied. The file header and the note in `action-execution.ts` now say the same.
- **B. Closed.** `approval-request-schema-party-read.dogfood.test.ts` now pins:
  - every member is served the request definition;
  - the action log and the undeclared sibling still answer `404` to a member party to no request;
  - the approver's object list is that member's plus the action log;
  - the approver reads their own request by id, and the action log's rows stay refused;
  - the non-party is served no row, and `404` by id.

  The PR body carries the paragraph round 1 asked for. 1B supersedes two terms of 6840464379: the request rows closed to members on the data door, and the request definition reaching only a party through the delegate. `sys_approval_action` stands as decided, and the delegate stays on both objects. Run in the probe build on this head: this file and `approval-read-over-mcp.dogfood.test.ts`, 10 tests, all passed.
- **C. GHSA-2985-5f64-8wgh: the must-fix stands. Security findings: 2, withheld (reported to the seat).**
- **C2. Holds.** `sys_approval_request` declares `enable.feeds: false`.
  - Pinned as a declaration in `sys-approval-request.object.test.ts` (the flag is `false`, `approval_comment` is declared). The refusal itself is plugin-audit's generic gate on `sys_comment` insert and update, pinned in the comments dogfood. Observed on the live stack in the probe: a `sys_comment` insert naming a request answers `403 FEEDS_DISABLED` for a party and for a non-party.
  - It breaks nothing read here. The request page declares no `record:discussion` node, plugin-approvals writes no `sys_comment`, and the console strips discussion nodes when the flag is off. `Test UI` and `Live E2E UI` are green.
  - What it does not do: the flag gates writes. A comment row already at rest on a request (only an administrator could have written one before 1B) is still served to whoever reads that request.
- **D. Closed in the PR's own files:** the schema-read note in `sys-approval-request.object.ts`, the no-middleware warning in `approvals-plugin.ts` (it now also says to withdraw the baseline line), the denied-load note in `action-execution.ts`, and both places in `approvals.mdx`. The spec prose in `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts` still says the request "is deliberately closed on the data side"; the PR body sends it to a follow-up and names no card.
- **E. Closed.** The HTTP bridge answers every `aiReadExposed` ask from one merged read (`mergedForAiRead`). The bridge is built per request, so the listing does not outlive the request; a failed read stays failed for that request, which `readGuard` reads as closed. Pinned: three asks, one `getMetaItems` call.
- **Round-1 nit. Closed.** The `query_records` text gives the approvals filter as an example.

**Red lines on the delta**

- The delta leaves `request-read-gate.ts`, `approval-service.ts`, `default-permission-sets.ts`, `stdio-data-bridge.ts` and every guard in `mcp-http-tools.ts` unchanged (the one changed line there is tool text). Round 1's ① 1 to 5 therefore carry to this head as written: no write opens on any `sys_*` object, no other `sys_*` object becomes readable, and 2B cannot widen.
- The three code additions narrow or cache; none admits anything. The plugin-audit change and `enable.feeds: false` each serve or accept less. `mergedForAiRead` is E above.
- Observed on the live stack in the probe, as plain members holding the shipped baseline. A member party to no request is served no request row, and `404` by id. For a party and a non-party alike: PATCH, DELETE and POST on the request answer `405`; `sys_approval_action`, `sys_approval_approver` and `sys_audit_log` answer `403`.

**Should-fix**

- **F. The changeset states the declaration, not its effect.** A reader of the CHANGELOG learns that the object "declares `enable.feeds: false`", not that a `sys_comment` write naming an approval request is now refused `403 FEEDS_DISABLED`. Say so in the changeset (a prose face).

**Nit**

- In `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts`, the new `mergedForAiRead` declaration sits between `readServedObject` and that function's docblock.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset adds `@objectstack/plugin-audit` at `patch`. It now names the five published packages the diff moves: `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`. `packages/verify` moves a test file only, and the dogfood package is private. `Check Changeset` is green.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is still right. `enable.feeds` is a published key with this meaning; a platform object setting it adds nothing an author can write. `none` takes `patch`.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)`: round 1 wrote "nothing narrows", and that no longer holds for the whole diff. The delta adds two changes that narrow. The comment door now refuses a request as a target for every caller, an administrator included, whose same write `main` accepts; and the plugin-audit change serves less. Both are runtime permission and security behaviour, which the fleet's rule keeps outside clause ② and with the human floor (`references/execution-duties.md`). So the line still describes the diff's clause-② content, and this record stays on the declaration face. Whether the comment-door refusal is a breaking narrowing that owes the changeset a BREAKING banner and an ADR-0087 disposition is the seat's call with triage, before the next head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Flags travel with the withheld findings (reported to the seat).
- **The human floor.** Rulings 6837430865 and 6849636735 cover the read admission, 1B and 2B. No ruling on the card names `enable.feeds` on this object: the seat decided it in round 1. The seat's ACCEPT should name it, or take it to the maintainer.
- **No report for this head is on the card.** The last `os-dev-report` (6856567007) is the round-1 one. The fix report reached this review as a seat file, so its `open_questions` and `security_findings` lines cannot be read from the public thread.
- **Claim.** Re-post 6857527959 covers every file of the delta: the plugin-audit file, the warning text, the runtime prose, the two moved suites, the `feeds` declaration, the tests beside each, the docs page and the changeset. `PR-body guards` are green.
- **Verification claims against the head.** The PR body's suites ran on `dbd75155f3`; `8e4da801d2` after it changes one warning string (read). The ablation table's row C is the dev's and was not re-run here.
- **Dogfood.** The PR lanes skip the dogfood shards. The two approval files ran green in the probe build; the other 17 files the body lists did not run here.
- **CI on this head at writing:** 38 check-runs green, 17 skipped, none red. `Test Core (1/8)` was still in progress; the other seven shards are green, and so are the two lanes round 1 found red.
- The PR is a draft and no auto-merge is armed. Author: the PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.
- No `Contract-review-claim:` line names this head; this record is the first to name it.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-bb7kzf`
Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4cwJbS8sZAfru2iyvQq`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

Must-fix: C (GHSA-2985-5f64-8wgh, withheld). Should-fix: F. Closed from round 1: A, B, C2, D, E. A delta review by the same reviewer is owed on the next head.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `a12e7c9c9b7d830c6e26a91e777af818dea41159`
Local-runs: probe — GHSA-2985-5f64-8wgh: round 2 failed on it, and the diff and the check-runs cannot show on a live stack that its fix on this head is complete. One throwaway test file on the PR's own dogfood rig, in a detached checkout of this head, deleted after the run; the worktree is clean and nothing was committed. The same build ran the four dogfood files and five plugin-audit unit files named under ③.

This is a DELTA record on round 2 (6859509619, FAIL at `8e4da801d2`); round 1 is 6857191533. It judges `git diff 8e4da801d2 a12e7c9c9b` (two commits, 13 files) and the code that diff touches, against round 2's open items and round 1's red lines, and says nothing about a later head. Face: declaration, unchanged. The file list carries no published-schema or governed path, and the changeset and the PR body carry `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. Rendered by an isolated sub-agent of this seat. Inputs: rounds 1 and 2, the claim re-post 6857527959, the PR body as refreshed for this head, the delta, the seat's brief, and the check-runs on this head. Code outside the diff was read, never reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

**Round-2 items**

- **C. GHSA-2985-5f64-8wgh: closed on this head. Security findings on the delta: 0.**
